title: Knowledge check: Parsing JSON Request Bodies

questions.prompt: In Parsing JSON Request Bodies, which statement best describes Configuring express.json()?
options: Connect this syllabus point to Parsing JSON Request Bodies: state the expected behavior, identify a realistic edge case, and choose a test or observation that proves the behavior instead of relying on assumptions.

questions.prompt: Which design rule is most appropriate when applying Parsing JSON Request Bodies?
options: Trust request fields and skip authorization to keep handlers small.
Suppress all errors without recording safe diagnostic information.
Assume that adding CORS makes private routes authenticated.

Request bodies, parameters, and query strings arrive as untrusted values. Parse only the expected content type, enforce size limits, validate and normalize data, and return consistent client errors before business logic runs.
questions.answer_key: Request bodies, parameters, and query strings arrive as untrusted values. Parse only the expected content type, enforce size limits, validate and normalize data, and return consistent client errors before business logic runs.

questions.prompt: A change related to Parsing JSON Request Bodies appears to work for one normal request. What is the strongest next verification step?
options: Use production data to avoid building a small reproducible fixture.
Treat the page’s displayed reference output as proof that Node.js executed the code.
Use repeatable tests for a successful request and at least one invalid/boundary or dependency-failure case.
Test only one successful request manually and record no expected output.
